mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30 days prior to the rate increase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by declining unemployment (UNRATE) creates a labor market momentum that elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% while PAYEMS increases by at least 2,000 in a month
failure_condition: In 80% of similar labor expansion episodes since 2000, 20-day forward returns underperform the preceding 5-day average return (Rank IC > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a shift from supply-side to demand-side driven market expansion, predicting positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 10% in a month while INDPRO decreases by > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: Over 12 months of backtests, demand-supply divergence events produce no statistically significant positive 5-day forward returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 for three consecutive months indicates a supply-side bottleneck that raises uncertainty and depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO remains below 105 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: During 3 prior comparable contractions, 20-day forward returns averaged 0.1% with standard deviation 2.5%, and 20-day returns during the current event do not fall below the 2.5th percentile (quantile regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% in a single month triggers a risk-off reaction that drives S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by > 0.5% in a single month
failure_condition: In 15 historical inflation shocks since 1980, only 2 produced negative 20-day forward returns when CPI fell > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 4% for two consecutive months, the tight labor market encourages firms to increase investment in growth-oriented equities, predicting positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 10 historical episodes of double-digit monthly UNRATE declines below 4%, 60-day forward returns averaged 0.2% with 95% CI [-0.5%, 0.9%].

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 and a sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% jointly predict a bullish sentiment that drives S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 200,000 for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE falls below 5% for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: robust consumer demand and labor market strength
failure_condition: In 50 analogous historical combinations of high PAYEMS growth and low UNRATE, 5-day forward returns averaged -0.1% (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) below 450 million dollars for four consecutive months indicates a structural supply shock that depresses investor confidence and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS remains below 450 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: During 7 prior multi-month RSAFS contractions, 60-day forward returns averaged -0.8% with 95% CI [-1.2%, -0.4%]; current event does not exceed the upper bound.
